body:
The provisions of subdivisions 67:46:14:02(3) and (4) do not apply if any of the following circumstances exist:

(1) The child had coverage under a group health plan and the coverage was dropped for good cause;

(2) The child had health insurance coverage or was covered under a group health plan but access to care was not available under the policy; or

(3) The child has health insurance coverage or is covered under a group health plan but access to care is not available under the policy.

Source: 26 SDR 168, effective July 1, 2000.

General Authority: SDCL 28-6-1.

Law Implemented: SDCL 28-6-1.

Example: If a child's absent parent is located in another state and covers the child through the parent's employer's health maintenance organization and the child cannot get treatment in South Dakota under the policy, the coverage is considered to be inaccessible to the child.

body:
The department may request information from any member of a children's health insurance program (CHIP-NM) family concerning the existence of actual or potential third-party liability coverage or a third-party payment source for medical expenses. For purposes of this section , third-party liability coverage or a third-party payment source is the obligation of an entity other than the medical assistance program for either partial or full payment of the medical cost of injury, disease, or disability for the child .

The caretaker must provide the department with the necessary verifications to establish initial or continuing eligibility and any information necessary for federal reporting requirements or quality control efforts. The department shall deny an application for CHIP-NM or terminat e current benefits for failure or refusal to supply the necessary verifications or information .

An alien who fails or refuses to obtain the cooperation of the alien's sponsor is ineligible for assistance.

Source: 26 SDR 168, effective July 1, 2000; 41 SDR 7, effective July 29, 2014 ; 51 SDR 52, effective November 11, 2024 .

General Authority: SDCL 28-6-1 .

Law Implemented: SDCL 28-6-1 .

Cross-Reference: Acceptance of assistance as assignment and subrogation of support rights and insurance proceeds--Liability of insurer or attorney, SDCL 28-6-7.1 .

body:
Terms used in this chapter mean:

(1) "Caretaker relative," a relative of a dependent child by blood, adoption, or marriage with whom the child is living, who assumes primary responsibility for the child's care (as may, but is not required to, be indicated by claiming the child as a tax dependent for Federal income tax purposes), and who is one of the following:

(a) The child's father, mother, grandfather, grandmother, brother, sister, stepfather, stepmother, stepbrother, stepsister, uncle, aunt, first cousin, nephew, or niece;

(b) The spouse of such parent or relative, even after the marriage is terminated by death or divorce.

(2) "Dependent child," a child who has not attained 18 years of age or has not attained 19 years of age and is a full-time student in a secondary school, and is expected to complete the program before reaching the age of 19;

(3) "Parent," a natural or biological, adoptive or step parent;

(4) "Pregnant woman," a woman during pregnancy and the post-partum period, which begins on the date the pregnancy ends, extends 60 days, and ends on the last day of the month in which the 60-day period ends; and

(5) "Family Size/Household," an individual's family size has the same meaning as determined under the provisions of 42 C.F.R. § 435.603 (July 15, 2013).

Source: 24 SDR 24, effective August 31, 1997; 41 SDR 7, effective July 29, 2014.

General Authority: SDCL 28-6-1.

Law Implemented: SDCL 28-6-1.

Cross-References: Definitions and use of terms, 42 C.F.R. § 435.4 (March 23, 2012); Application of modified adjusted gross income (MAGI), 42 C.F.R. § 435.603 (July 15, 2013).

(1) They meet the general eligibility requirements of chapter 67:46:01;

(2) They meet the requirements contained in this chapter.
